newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore cuts ministers', senior bureaucrats' pay.
newsitem.headline: Singapore cuts ministers', senior bureaucrats' pay.

text.p: Singapore's ministers and senior bureaucrats, among the world's best paid, will have their salaries cut from July 1 to keep them in line with the private sector, the government said on Wednesday.
The pay cut will be between two and seven percent, depending on the grade, and will apply to political, statutory, judiciary and parliamentary office holders, it said in a statement.

Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong currently makes more than Singapore $1.2 million (US$850,000) and Singapore's top ministers and civil servants also earn several times more than their counterparts in the United States, Japan and Europe.
The government said junior grade ministers would get S$36,200 a month after the change, down seven percent.
Bureaucrats at the most junior grade in the administrative service would get S$12,900, down two percent, it said.

This is the first time the government has cut salaries of ministers and senior officers since it adopted a formula in 1994 linking their pay levels to wages of top private sector executives, a government spokesman told Reuters.

The statement said the revisions were based on 1995 income data which showed the average principal earned income of the top four individuals from selected private sector professions had fallen by 18 percent.
Singapore officials believe the city state's high government salaries help maintain honest leadership and prevent talent from being drained away by the booming private sector.
